why: I checked each verifier PASS/FAIL condition against the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2 and 4 only test what their lines say: padLeft is exported, pads on the left with a space by default, returns s unchanged at or over width, and npm test exits 0 with no failures. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition also requires that "the exports list includes at least capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft." Line 3 only says that every function index.js exports has a README section. It doesn't say which functions must still be exported. Requiring that capitalize, slugify and truncate remain exported is a preservation rule the words don't force, and the brief itself lists "existing ... functions were left intact" as Advisory. Because that stricter requirement sits inside a PASS condition rather than under Advisory, the criterion fails.
